decisions.reason: A newly launched handle family that needed tooling and finishing investment and fits the firm's coordinated product-family strategy, so one year of modest visibility is read as normal ramp-up.
The mitred handle line represents committed design and production investment and extends the architecture-aware range, so management will give it more time to gain specifications.
A multifunctional handle supports the barrier-free, one-stop direction the firm has announced, which makes dropping it after one year inconsistent with its stated strategy.
Sunk costs in tooling and the long specification cycles typical of architectural hardware justify keeping this handle line despite its limited visibility so far.
The collection has its own page and a German Design Award, a strong public commitment that makes its withdrawal very unlikely.
A finish option adds little ongoing cost, is used across the existing families, and supports the firm's premium metal-finishing identity.
